description:
dev/studies/b488f02c/throughput-2026-08-07.csv carries two measured cells whose repetition counts violate the protocol the study states (at least 5 repetitions and 5 s of timed work under a 120 s cap): q=5, n=28, cpu_rayon_batch_scalar at one repetition of ~148 s, and q=3, n=28, gpu_hip M=1024 at three repetitions. The feasibility-study section 4.4 table publishes the q=5 cell's 0.648 without qualification.

## Background

Found by the F_5 receipt campaign (91605d4d, receipts section 14): both offending cells are ones the campaign reruns censor under the same rule, and the q=5 cell is load-bearing for cross-run comparison — it makes the prior best CPU path at n=28 appear 14.3x faster than what the rule-conformant rerun measures. The campaign receipts already record the discrepancy; this issue owns the correction at the source.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The feasibility study identifies each published cell that does not meet the stated repetition/censoring rule and marks it as protocol-nonconforming where it is rendered, or removes it from the rendered table, without altering the committed CSV.
- [hard] REQ-02: The recorded check in the study directory (or a companion check) verifies that every rendered throughput cell either satisfies the stated stopping rule or carries the nonconformance marker.

## Notes

The committed CSV is a faithful record of what ran and is not edited (falsification-preserved); the defect is the unqualified rendering. Related: a2c0db52 (rounding discrepancies in the same table).
title: Prior throughput grid publishes rates its stated stopping rule forbids
